tools.name: check_robots
tools.description: Match a robots.txt file the caller pastes against Botcard's AI crawler tokens, using RFC 9309. Each row is allow or disallow plus that token's vendor stance. This tool does not fetch any website. Do not send url, host, target, website, robots_url, or fetch.

tools.name: list_crawlers
tools.description: List the AI crawler robots.txt tokens in this dataset. Each row names the vendor page the summary was checked against. This tool does not fetch any website. Do not send url, host, target, website, robots_url, or fetch.

tools.name: get_crawler
tools.description: Return one card by id, including the vendor source URL and the date it was read. This tool does not fetch any website. Do not send url, host, target, website, robots_url, or fetch.

tools.name: suggest_robots
tools.description: Write a robots.txt from this dataset for the kinds you allow or block. Each group cites the vendor page. effect request_only means the vendor does not say the crawler obeys that line. control_token is not training. The file has no User-agent: * group. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_robots, list_crawlers, get_crawler, suggest_robots · Private data: check_robots, list_crawlers, suggest_robots · Public sink: check_robots, list_crawlers, get_crawler, suggest_robots.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_robots, list_crawlers, get_crawler, suggest_robots · Private data: check_robots, list_crawlers, suggest_robots · Public sink: check_robots, list_crawlers, get_crawler, suggest_robots

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
